key_insight: Detonation-sprayed self-fluxing Ni–Cr–Fe–B–Si–C coatings can be tuned from low-friction to high-wear-resistance behavior by adjusting barrel filling, gas ratio, and inter-shot delay.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a process window for restoring and hardening machine parts with coatings whose density, hardness, roughness, and tribology can be traded off for the target service condition.
method: Changed inter-shot delay from 0–1 s during detonation spraying
evidence_signal: Evaluation combined microstructural inspection, roughness measurement, hardness testing, and tribological tests; best wear rate reached 0.000189 mm³/(N·m), while minimum friction was μ = 0.674 ± 0.136.
watch_item: Optimizing for friction reduction and optimizing for wear resistance do not occur under the same spray settings, so process selection must match the intended operating load.
paper_title: Development of a Method for Producing Self-Fluxing Nickel-Based Coatings by Detonation Spraying
